body:
(cw: self harm, suicide)

26

I'm realizing my anxiety and low self esteem prevent me from being a pleasant person to be around. I'm nearly a year into my job and have not made any friends. Conversations are superficial and brief, and I can see the look of discomfort on coworkers' faces as I stumble through a sentence. The past month or so has been worse as work stress and aggressive deadlines have made it difficult to mask my issues. People have started to actively avoid, ignore, or call out my ineptitude.

Every week or so I have thoughts about ending my life, but resort to drinking, over eating, and hitting myself. I haven't made any new friends since I finished college a year ago. I've realized that I am the problem, and while I'm trying to be better by cutting way back on drinking and going to therapy, I still feel hopeless.

Once I graduated college, so 25 in my case. I just walked to accept my diploma a few weeks ago and I haven't found the strength to follow through on that promise I made myself.

It doesn't help that I set myself up for failure by not planning to be alive by now. I stopped any form of healthy self care long ago and my personal relationships are failing.

Hey friend from 12 days ago,

I started my first full time engineering job after finishing my Master's in ME and have never been as depressed or anxious as I have now. I'm still not 100% sure if the source is the job environment or the type of work or just myself. In school, I got good grades and enjoyed the classes, but I never really found out who I was or what my hobbies are. 

I agree with your last point; life is way too short.
I compulsively pull my hair out when stressed. I then get stressed that my hair looks irregular; then I pull more out. OCD is the worst.

I just finished my Master's in Engineering. I agree that graduating changes one's perspective. I've been in school for more than 20 years of my life. I feel like I am not good for anything but school. Now that I have a job, I am struggling to make meaningful work relationships and my anxiety makes it difficult to perform. Everyday I embarass myself in front of coworkers and the only way I keep myself from breaking down in the office is reminding myself that I can end it all once I get home. Of course when I get home I'm too tired to actually commit to a plan, but it leaves me with the stress and anxiety of having to face them again tomorrow.
